description: Baseline: default architecture, no weight assignment (random init); used to inspect the task interface.
2 blocks: shift-register attention + conjunction MLP tags field terminators; output steps query roles and copy window digits.
role-pointer-v1 with the NULL register moved to the '=' token, whose 4-token window is always padding even for the longest 27-char dates.
Removes the unused MLP from block 2, so the second block is a pure attention lookup.
Replaces one-hot tokens with a readable 14-dim code (digit nibble, letter index, punctuation flags) and nearest-code output decoding; d_model 248 -> 72.
nibble-code-v1 with a +1 logit bias on output tokens, so digit 0 no longer ties with every unused token.
Drops the dedicated NULL slot: the step-0 position bit already marks '=', so idle heads key on it.
Drops the dedicated DASH slot: the unembedding reads the '-' logit straight from the step-4 and step-7 position bits.
Drops the PROMPT slot, computing it linearly as ON minus the step bits; d_model 72 -> 68.
Decouples head width from d_model: block 1 heads are 13-dim and block 2 heads 8-dim, shrinking the attention matrices.
Separates key and value widths per block: block 1 uses 2-dim keys (position circle) with 11-dim values; block 2 uses 4-dim role keys with 4-dim nibble values.
Removes the word-like SEP flag: the day rule becomes a digit followed by anything except a digit, slash, dot or padding; d_model 66.
Replaces the first-slash neuron: every '/' is a MONTH key and the second-slash neuron cancels it; d_ff 18.
Letters share the digit nibble (low 4 bits plus one high bit); trigram neurons replace the known letter bits with the month digits; d_model 54.
Sharpness sweep: shift-register key scale B1 lowered from 200 to 60 (neighbour-position score gap about 12).
Sharpness sweep: B1 = 30 (neighbour-position score gap about 3), to find where shift-register leakage breaks the rules.
Tightens the position circle from period 64 to 48 at B1 = 30, nearly doubling the gap between adjacent positions (about 5.5).
Sharpness sweep: block 2 role query scale B2 lowered from 300 to 30, matching B1 (role score gap 15).
Drops the letter high bit: letters are their alphabet index mod 16, testing whether month trigrams stay unambiguous; d_model 51.
YEAR rule now needs only three digits before a non-digit token, removing the offset-4 digit flag; d_model 50.
The yy century override only pushes the low two bits (+2/-2). Failed: it assumed offset 4 held the day's tens digit, but it holds the ones digit, whose high bits leak into the century.
Restores the 4-bit century override (offset 4 is the day's ones digit) and removes the ON slot via rule thresholds and a real head bias; d_model 49.
Removes the three is-digit guards from each trigram neuron, testing whether digit runs ever imitate a month's bit pattern.
Keeps one is-digit guard per trigram neuron (offset 1), which blocks the digit collision found in v5 where years ending in 35 hashed to 'sep'.
Moves the single trigram guard to offset 2, which vetoes both digit collisions found so far: '35_' as 'sep' and '1/2' as 'apr'.
Sharpness sweep: B2 = 10 (role score gap 5 against about 40 other positions), to find the limit of the role lookup.
Sharpness sweep: B1 = 22 on the period-48 circle (neighbour gap about 3), to compare with the failure at gap 3 on the period-64 circle.
Round scales with margin above the failures at B1 = 22: B1 = 40 and B2 = 20. Base model for the ablation series.
Ablation of hash-nibble-v10: disables the mm/dd/yy year rule, which should cost only that format's share.
Ablation of hash-nibble-v10: disables the four-digit year rule, which should break every format except mm/dd/yy.
Ablation of hash-nibble-v10: disables the second-dot month rule, which should break only yyyy.mm.dd.
Ablation of hash-nibble-v10: disables the second-slash rule, which should break both day and month across the two slash formats.
Ablation of hash-nibble-v10: disables the yyyy.mm.dd end-of-string day rule, which should break only that format's day.
Ablation of hash-nibble-v10: disables the general day rule, which should break all six month-word formats but neither slash nor dotted dates.
Ablation of hash-nibble-v10: disables all 12 trigram neurons, which should break only the month field in the six month-word formats.

Ablation of hash-nibble-v10: removes the BOS token, so offsets past the start of the string clamp onto token 0 and single-digit leading fields read a wrong tens digit. Cost more than predicted: clamped digits also trigger false YEAR tags.
Ablation of hash-nibble-v10 (BOS restored): removes the causal mask, testing whether the backward-looking circuit relies on it during prefix-only generation.
Restores the causal mask. Derives the year's second digit from the low bit of the first (1 gives 9, 2 gives 0), dropping the offset-3 nibble; d_model 45.
Stores only the two low bits at offset 4, since the century digit is 1 or 2; the yy override then needs just those two bits; d_model 43.
Shrinks the answer-step veto: none on YEAR (its only false tag comes after the year is written) and just two steps on the general day rule.
Block 2 keys shrink from 4 to 2 dims: YEAR, MONTH, DAY and NULL sit at the four compass points, so a mismatched role scores zero or below.
Narrows the tables to the slots they use: 8-dim token table, 12-dim position table, and a 6-input head; same computation, fewer unused zero parameters.
Trigram neurons keep only their positive inputs (bits that must be on), testing whether the 'must be off' inputs are needed.
Reads the century from one bit at offset 3: set for 19xx, clear for 20xx and for the '/' of mm/dd/yy, so yy needs no override and block 1 drops its fourth head; d_model 42.
One key per token shared by all heads in a block: heads differ only in their query, removing duplicated key weights.
Rules write role directions straight into two key slots (east YEAR, north MONTH, west DAY), replacing three role slots; d_model 41.
Block 2 sums its heads before W_o, since all four write the same output bits: one copy of the wiring instead of four.
Position circle period equals the sequence length (43 with BOS): one point per position, no magic constant, and a wider gap between neighbours.
Margin check on the fully reduced circuit: lowers B1 to 30 and B2 to 10 to see how close the chosen scales (40, 20) are to failure.
Final circuit (B1 = 40, B2 = 20) with the development check widened to 100,000 fresh dates over 20 unseen seeds, to catch rare hash collisions.
Final clean circuit: 3-head shift register, 18 conjunction neurons tagging field terminators with compass directions, then a 4-head role lookup; d_model 41.
